what_the_eye_sees: A lizard crawling over a plain polished half-round band, with a small orange stone set in bare metal in front of its head. The skin is uniformly pebbled, like a toad or a generic lizard, and it shows no pattern. The left third is a lumpy, ridged mass where body, legs and tail wrap over the shoulder and down the side, so no clear tail shape shows. The head is small and hard to separate from the forelegs. The right 40% of the face and the whole shank are bare. A jeweller would say 'lizard', perhaps 'baby croc' or 'gecko', but not Gila monster: nothing here is specific to Heloderma. The fat tail, the broad blunt head and the banded beadwork are all missing.

changes.what: Put the Gila's banding into the beadwork: alternate high-bead and low-bead transverse bands across the back and tail, so that dark and light stripes read at 300 px.
changes.where: Across the whole dorsal surface of the lizard, from the nape to the tail tip: about 4 bands on the trunk and 4 to 5 rings on the tail, with forked, reticulated edges.
changes.by_how_much: Bands 1.5 to 2.0 mm wide. High beads 0.40 mm, low beads 0.18 to 0.20 mm (at least 0.20 mm apart; the planned 0.36/0.24 is too subtle). Recess the low bands' lands a further 0.1 mm so the oxide or shadow holds, and check that the stripes are countable in face-300.png.

changes.what: Rebuild the tail as the Gila's short, swollen fat-store: a thick sausage with a blunt tip, lying on the face instead of disappearing over the left shoulder into the side.
changes.where: From the hips back along the crest toward theta 60 to 90, on the face and upper shoulder, visible in both hero and face views.
changes.by_how_much: Tail width at the base at least 75% of the trunk width, tapering by no more than 30% before a rounded tip. Length about 40% of the snout-to-vent length. It must read as one clean silhouette against the bare band in face-300.png.

changes.what: Make the head broad, flat and blunt, clearly separate from the forelimbs, and give the legs a short, stubby Gila stance. Then let the beaded hide carry onto the empty right side of the face and the shoulders, so the body does not sit on bare stock.
changes.where: Head and forelimbs near the stone. The bare face and shoulder from roughly theta 90 to 150 around the stone.
changes.by_how_much: Head width about 85% of the neck width, with a rounded, nearly square snout (no taper to a point) and a 0.3 mm neck crease behind it. Leg length at most 50% of the body depth. Low beads (0.15 to 0.20 mm) cover at least 70% of the currently bare face area, with the stone seated in the bead field.
